title: An Afternoon in the Archive
paragraphs: During an afternoon at a community archive, a class examined records of ordinary experiences. Some came from personal journals, while others resembled reports or scenes from fiction. The students agreed that useful evidence could come from a quiet incident as well as a surprising one.

The group began by reading the following accounts without adding explanations of its own. A grimace crossed his face as he tasted the bitter drink. The grizzled sailor watched the approaching storm. His gruff reply sounded harsher than he intended. The store offered a guarantee against defects.

It then considered a second group of accounts, looking for both similarities and differences. The history described a guerrilla hiding in the mountain forests. Without measurements, the cost was only a guesstimate. We needed evidence rather than guesswork to solve the problem. The beginners completed the task with careful guidance.

The class finished by comparing its first impressions with its later interpretations. Some ideas had survived closer examination; others needed to be revised. The students kept the original details visible so that future readers could judge for themselves. They understood that a convincing explanation should connect the evidence clearly while leaving room for questions the records could not answer.

targets.definition: a facial expression showing pain, disgust, or discomfort
having gray or partly gray hair
rough and abrupt in voice or manner
a firm promise that something will happen or be provided
a member of a small irregular force using surprise attacks
an estimate made with limited information
judgment based on guesses rather than firm knowledge
help or advice about what to do
